jobs.title: Housing Specialist
jobs.description:
Requirements

Bachelor’s degree preferred in Human Services, Social Work, Psychology, or a related field; or a high school diploma/equivalent with work experience supporting adults with serious mental illness or individuals with similar human-services needs.
Experience working with individuals experiencing homelessness.
Valid driver’s license required; ability to travel throughout Beaver County to provide community-based support.

Are you looking for an opportunity to advance your career while working with an extraordinary team? At Merakey, we put heart and soul into everything we do.

We are seeking a Housing Specialist
to join our team in our Monaca, PA location covering Beaver County
.

Earn $23.83/hour + mileage reimbursement

Position Details

The Housing Specialist within the ACT team is instrumental in meeting the housing requirements of individuals with co-occurring disorders. Working closely with Psychiatrists and Primary Care Physicians, the Housing Specialist aids in treatment planning by evaluating the influence of addiction on mental and physical health and aiding in decision-making processes. Responsibilities encompass advising on medication prescriptions for substance abuse disorders, evaluating physical health, and orchestrating medical, psychiatric, and substance abuse treatments. By ensuring consumers have stable housing, the Housing Specialist significantly bolsters the efficacy of the ACT program, ultimately promoting overall recovery and well-being.

Assists consumers with housing needs, including searches, budgeting, and applications.
Builds relationships with housing vendors and facilitates referrals.
Supports lease agreements, deposits, and budgeting with consumers and payers.
Acts as a liaison between individuals and landlords to resolve issues.
Collaborates with the team on housing goals and participates in treatment meetings.
Completes assessments, provides cross-training, and fulfills on-call duties as assigned.

Our Assertive Community Treatment (ACT) model supports individuals with serious mental illnesses who may not have experienced success or haven't found effective support within traditional outpatient programs. We offer tailored services emphasizing relationship-building and active involvement in enhancing functioning and symptom management.

Services involve weekly home visits, provided either in individuals' residences or within the community, utilizing personal vehicles for client transportation and community-based tasks.

If you are enthusiastic about making a positive impact on individuals facing mental health challenges and wish to be part of a collaborative and supportive team, apply now to join our essential ACT Team at Merakey. Together, we can contribute to the journey of recovery.

Benefits

Merakey offers generous benefits that promote well-being, financial security, and work-life balance, including:

Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus access to healthcare advocacy support.
Retirement plan -- both pre-tax and Roth (after-tax) options available for employee contributions.
DailyPay -- access your pay when you need it!
On the Goga well-being platform, featuring self-care tools and resources.
Access Care.com for backup childcare, elder care, and household services.
Confidential counseling, legal, and financial services through our Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
Tuition reimbursement and educational partnerships.
Employee discounts and savings programs on entertainment, travel, and lifestyle.
Access to Pryor Online Learning for free online personal development classes.

Learn more about our full benefits package - https://www.merakey.org/careers/benefits

jobs.title: Community Case Manager
jobs.description:
Requirements

The ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in human services field combined with experience working within the mental health field.
Valid LA Driver’s License
Must have state and federal clearances.

Are you looking for an opportunity to advance your career while working with an extraordinary team? At Merakey, we put heart and soul into everything we do.

We are seeking a Case Manager
to join our team in our Shreveport, LA location.

Earn: $22.67/hour + $7,500/yearly mileage stipend

Position Details

The Community Case Manager is responsible for treatment planning and providing face to face and telehealth case management services for the Nursing Home Diversion and Transition Case Management. This position is responsible for managing an assigned caseload of clients having severe mental illness and for assessing client needs, developing, implementing, and reviewing service plans, and working with other community resources in meeting/achieving client service needs.

General Duties And Responsibilities

Participates as directed in the screening of new service requests within the clinic by means of and agency approved procedure which ensures that all individuals are adequately and appropriately served according to their individual needs and in accordance with existing policies and procedures.
Coordinates case management assessment on all clients entering caseload.
Develops appropriate treatment/service plans with clients as the means for implementing appropriate services and developing effective alliances with clients.
Provides on-going supportive and/or case management functions in accordance with the problems, needs, and the strategies identified within the service plan to help the clients to achieve the stated goals and objectives.
Provides face to face reviews with the client and/or relevant staff on a regular basis the progress made in reaching service goals so that the service plan can be modified as necessary to ensure that the goals and objectives are being achieved. The frequency reviews will be determined by relevant requirements.
Documents all service contacts on a timely basis including face-to-face interviews, collateral and networking contacts, correspondence and maintains the case records in accordance with agency and regulatory standards and requirements.
Participates in planning and service coordination activities as directed to improve and enhance service continuity and effectiveness for clients.
Complete required productivity, mileage and other reports in a timely fashion as required.
Meets regularly with the immediate supervisor as a means of enhancing professional growth, reviewing and processing the provision of case management services, and dealing with appropriate administrative issues.
Maintains close communication with the consulting Nurse Program Director for input regarding medication compliance, side effects of medication, and medication changes and alerts these members of the staff of any changes in client adjustment which might suggest decompensation and a need for more aggressive intervention.
Maintains service logs and turns them in on a weekly basis so that staff and client service information can be reviewed by supervisors and management personnel and can be reported to local and state funding sources to determine if performance contract levels of service have been achieved and/or maintained.

jobs.title: Shelter Supervisor
jobs.description:
Summary

A supervisory position working with dependent and alleged delinquent youth and Youth and Family Advocates (YFAs) in a non-secure residential setting. Responsible for the training and supervision of the YFAs, for the maintenance of the program and for fostering good child-care practices. Must be familiar with the Child Protective Services Law, the Juvenile Act, and Article 3800 regulations of the Department of Human Services.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Responsible for the quality of care administered to the residents by the Youth & Family Advocates.
Ensures that staff and residents adhere to all policies and procedures of the facility.
Ensures that all incidents are reviewed, investigated and documented properly.
Plans and supervises youth and staff in daily living activities including, but not limited to, recreation, education, resident employment program, meals, etc.
Monitors and coordinates the development of structured programs for youths.
Responsible for the training of new shelter employees and student interns.
Reports to the Shelter Administrator any infractions of Youth Center policies.
Ensures the safety and well-being of the program for both youth and employees.
Maintains and enforces mandated ratios being met as outlined by state regulations.
Supervises staff and youth during all structured activities and programs.
Participate in evaluating employee work performances and personnel actions.
Performs related work as required.

Qualification Requirements

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Bachelor's degree in social sciences and at least two (2) years' experience as a Youth & Family Advocate or social services field. Supervisory experience preferred.
Ability to guide, mentor and supervise youths and employees effectively.
Must be physically capable of handling adolescents during crisis situations using established procedures.
Ability to recognize situational problems and formulate new plans.
Must obtain a physical examination report from a licensed physician.
Must work rotating shifts, holidays and weekends.
Must have ability to complete and maintain records; express oneself well, both verbally and in writing.
Ability to maintain harmonious relationships with public and other employees.
Must have a valid drivers' license.
Must submit clearances (PA State Police, Child Abuse, FBI).
Must submit to pre-employment drug screening.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand; walk; sit; and talk and hear. The employee is occasionally required to use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools or controls; reach with hands or arms; and stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25pounds.Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision and depth perception.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential function.

The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Position Summary

NeuLife Rehabilitation is seeking a Program Manager
to oversee daily operations of our Bowling Green program. This role ensures high-quality care delivery, staff coordination, and operational support within a neuro-rehabilitation setting serving individuals with traumatic brain injuries and neurological conditions.

The Program Manager reports directly to the Executive Director
and operates under their direction. This role is responsible for executing program operations in alignment with the Executive Director's guidance, priorities, and expectations.

Key Responsibilities

Execute day-to-day program operations under the direction of the Executive Director
Coordinate and oversee therapy schedules and programming logistics
Manage appointments, calendars, and service coordination for persons served
Oversee and coordinate transportation for persons served, ensuring timeliness and safety
Supervise, coach, and support direct care and support staff
Ensure compliance with state, federal, and accreditation standards (CARF preferred)
Monitor staffing schedules, coverage, and daily operational needs
Support implementation of program initiatives and operational goals set by the Executive Director
Address employee relations matters in partnership with HR and leadership
Maintain a safe, structured, and therapeutic environment for persons served
Track and report key operational metrics as directed

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree required (Healthcare Administration, Psychology, or related field preferred)
3+ years of leadership or supervisory experience in healthcare, behavioral health, or rehabilitation
Experience with TBI, neuro-rehabilitation, or similar populations strongly preferred
Strong organizational and coordination skills
Ability to follow direction while managing multiple operational priorities
Excellent communication and team collaboration skills

⸻

What We Offer

Competitive salary within range listed
Opportunity to make a meaningful impact in neuro-rehabilitation
Growth and advancement opportunities
Supportive, mission-driven culture

Position Details

The Housing Specialist within the ACT team is instrumental in meeting the housing requirements of individuals with co-occurring disorders. Working closely with Psychiatrists and Primary Care Physicians, the Housing Specialist aids in treatment planning by evaluating the influence of addiction on mental and physical health and aiding in decision-making processes. Responsibilities encompass advising on medication prescriptions for substance abuse disorders, evaluating physical health, and orchestrating medical, psychiatric, and substance abuse treatments. By ensuring consumers have stable housing, the Housing Specialist significantly bolsters the efficacy of the ACT program, ultimately promoting overall recovery and well-being.

Our Assertive Community Treatment (ACT) model supports individuals with serious mental illnesses who may not have experienced success or haven't found effective support within traditional outpatient programs. Services involve weekly home visits, provided either in individuals' residences or within the community, utilizing personal vehicles for client transportation and community-based tasks.

Summary

A supervisory position working with dependent and alleged delinquent youth and Youth and Family Advocates (YFAs) in a non-secure residential setting. Responsible for the training and supervision of the YFAs, for the maintenance of the program and for fostering good child-care practices. Must be familiar with the Child Protective Services Law, the Juvenile Act, and Article 3800 regulations of the Department of Human Services.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Responsible for the quality of care administered to the residents by the Youth & Family Advocates.
Ensures that staff and residents adhere to all policies and procedures of the facility.
Ensures that all incidents are reviewed, investigated and documented properly.
Plans and supervises youth and staff in daily living activities including, but not limited to, recreation, education, resident employment program, meals, etc.
Monitors and coordinates the development of structured programs for youths.
Responsible for the training of new shelter employees and student interns.
Reports to the Shelter Administrator any infractions of Youth Center policies.
Ensures the safety and well-being of the program for both youth and employees.
Maintains and enforces mandated ratios being met as outlined by state regulations.
Supervises staff and youth during all structured activities and programs.
Participate in evaluating employee work performances and personnel actions.
Performs related work as required.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Bachelor's degree in social sciences and at least two (2) years' experience as a Youth & Family Advocate or social services field. Supervisory experience preferred.
Ability to guide, mentor and supervise youths and employees effectively.

Ability to recognize situational problems and formulate new plans.

Must submit to pre-employment drug screening.
